html:
The Battle of Timor was fought from 1942 to 1943, when Japan invaded Timor and a small force of Australian and Dutch commandos fought on in the mountains with the help of Timorese.

Portuguese Timor was neutral, but Allied troops had landed there and Japan attacked. The commandos held out for a year, kept supplied from Darwin, before being withdrawn. Timorese who helped them, often boys called criados, faced Japanese reprisals.

Tens of thousands of Timorese died in the war and the famine that came with it. The memory of Timorese help shaped Australian feeling during the later Indonesian occupation. See Pacific War and Dili.
